qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Unrivaled scale economies across global distribution, $8B+ annual advertising, and retail shelf space dominance combined with Lindy brand equity across 20+ billion-dollar brands (Tide, Pampers, Gillette, Crest, Dawn). Proved pricing power through recent inflation cycles with cumulative price increases defending 23%+ ROIC and 23% operating margins. Primary threat is private-label trade-down during severe economic contractions.
qualitative.note: Archetypal global consumer staples fortress with 23% median ROIC, 97% Owner FCF conversion, and an AA-rated balance sheet with 1.4x debt/OE and 22.5x interest coverage. Structurally insulated across all 5 macrotrends with local-for-local manufacturing and essential daily use habits. Primary risk is private-label trade-down in severe economic recessions. qualitative.evidence:
Procter & Gamble demonstrates multi-decade compounding excellence across 5 core segments: Fabric & Home Care (~35% of sales, Tide/Ariel/Dawn/Bounty), Baby, Feminine & Family Care (~25%, Pampers/Always/Charmin), Beauty (~18%, Head & Shoulders/Pantene/Olay), Health Care (~14%, Crest/Oral-B/Vicks), and Grooming (~8%, Gillette/Venus).
1. Capital Efficiency: 10-year GAAP ROIC median of 23.2% (excluding non-cash 2018 Gillette impairment, ROIC has stayed between 22% and 26% every year since FY2019). Tangible operating ROIC exceeds 100%. Operating margin expanded from ~20% in 2016 to ~23% in 2025.
2. Pricing Power: Demonstrated sustained pricing power through the 2021-2024 inflationary surge, achieving mid-single-digit price realization annually with minimal volume elasticity and defending gross margins above 50%.
3. Cash Flow Conversion: FCF conversion over 10 years averages 95-100% of GAAP Net Income (FY2025 Owner FCF of $15.9B on $16.0B Net Income). Capex remains low and disciplined at 4-5% of net sales.
4. Capital Allocation & Balance Sheet: Total debt of $22.8B against $9.9B cash (net debt of $12.9B is <0.8x Net Income). Interest coverage of 22.5x ($19.7B EBIT / $877M interest). 68-year track record of consecutive annual dividend increases with steady counter-cyclical share repurchases shrinking share count ~1-2% annually. Following the 2015-2016 Coty divestitures and restructuring into 6 focused business units, management has maintained exceptional capital discipline under Jon Moeller and successor Shailesh Jejurikar.
